composition.story: A 4-token prompt generates 4 more tokens, one per step, using one layer and one head. Each new query must attend to every earlier key and value. Step through with the KV cache, then switch to Without cache: every step then recomputes K and V for the whole context. The Totals step compares Σn with P+G.

aha.observation: With the cache, each token's key and value are projected once (P+G = 8 rows). Without it, every step re-projects the whole context (Σn = 30 rows).

controls.label: Step
controls.presentation: Previous / Next buttons; names kept when disabled at the first and last step

controls.label: Cache mode
controls.presentation: Selects the variant. Same tokens and steps; changes the K/V rows recomputed and the attention scores counted

controls.label: Reset
controls.presentation: Returns to Prefill and to With KV cache

states.label: Prefill
states.sentence: Prefill: the prompt tokens are projected into keys and values once, stored in the cache, and predict “the”.
states.why: Every prompt token needs a key and value before the first prediction.

states.label: Decode 1
states.sentence: Decode: only “the” is projected; its query attends over cached keys and values to predict “mat”.
states.short: Only the new token is projected
states.why: Earlier keys and values are unchanged, so they are read from the cache.

states.label: Decode 2
states.sentence: Decode: only “mat” is projected and appended; the cache supplies every earlier key and value to predict “and”.
states.why: Each step appends a single key and value; nothing is recomputed.

states.label: Decode 3
states.sentence: Decode: only “and” is new work; attention still reads the whole cache to predict “purred”.
states.why: Caching saves projection work, not the need to attend over the full context.

states.label: Decode 4
states.sentence: Decode: only “purred” is projected; attention over the full cache predicts the final period.
states.why: Per-step projection cost stays constant while the context keeps growing.

states.label: Totals
states.sentence: Totals: with caching, K/V work grows linearly with token count; recomputing it every step grows quadratically.
states.why: Stored keys and values replace repeated projections of the same tokens.

readouts.label: K/V rows without cache, Σn for n=4..8

states.label: Prefill
states.sentence: Prefill: the prompt tokens are projected into keys and values, used once to predict “the”, then discarded.
states.why: Nothing is kept, so the next step must rebuild them.

states.label: Decode 1
states.sentence: Decode: all tokens through “the” are re-projected from scratch so the new query can attend; predicts “mat”.
states.why: Without stored keys and values, earlier tokens are recomputed to be attended.

states.label: Decode 2
states.sentence: Decode: the whole context through “mat” is re-projected again, repeating work already done; predicts “and”.
states.why: Earlier tokens' keys and values are identical to last step's.

states.label: Decode 3
states.sentence: Decode: every earlier key and value is recomputed once more before predicting “purred”.
states.why: Only the newest position's output is used; the rest is wasted work.

states.label: Decode 4
states.sentence: Decode: the full context is re-projected yet again before predicting the final period.
states.why: Each step's cost scales with the whole context length.

states.label: Totals
states.sentence: Totals: with caching, K/V work grows linearly with token count; recomputing it every step grows quadratically.
states.why: Each step redoes every earlier token's projection.

readouts.label: K/V rows without cache, Σn for n=4..8

1.reason: The fixed picture of tokens, projection, K/V stores, query and attention, with active regions per step, shows whether earlier K/V are reused or recomputed, which answers why caching saves work.

2.reason: The stepper rests on the Totals state, which carries the 30 vs 8 rows comparison, until the learner presses Next or changes mode, and nothing is timed.

3.reason: The mode select swaps the active token sets, the rows computed per step (1 vs n), and the cache contents (n vs 0), and the step control moves through different states with different readouts.

4.reason: Callout targets are declared region ids, the active lists drive the highlights, the ghost binds to previous.active, and the readouts bind to state.readouts, so every part traces to declared data.

6.reason: The story, the sentences, the region labels (K cache vs "K (discarded after step)") and the controls consistently name the same tokens, projection, cache and Totals step, apart from a minor "4 more tokens" vs 5 predictions mismatch.

7.reason: The detailed depth adds the per-step and cumulative row counts and the score formulas n(n+1)/2 vs n, which are the formula and count the mechanism needs, and the picture stays one fixed layout with a single active set.
